text:
Seattle's 6-1 win in Calgary was lopsided on the scoreboard, but the first period told a different story. CGY out-chanced SEA 0.93 to 0.44 in expected goals over those 20 minutes and still trailed 3-0. Jordan Eberle scored on a power play at 9:10, Vince Dunn followed 32 seconds later on a slap shot that carried just a 2% chance of going in, and Frederick Gaudreau made it 3-0 with 30 seconds left in the period.

Seattle took control from there. SEA's expected goals rose to 1.44 in the second and 1.85 in the third, against 0.87 and 0.73 for CGY. Chandler Stephenson made it 4-0 at 3:13 of the third, and Matty Beniers added a fifth 51 seconds later. Ryan Strome broke the shutout at 16:35, but Kaapo Kakko answered 26 seconds after that. Dunn finished with a goal and two assists, and Jared McCann had three assists, with SEA outchancing CGY 1.31 to 0.30 while he was on the ice.

The goaltending sharpened the gap. Dustin Wolf allowed 6 goals on 32 shots, about 2.3 more than the quality of those shots deserved, while Joey Daccord stopped 24 of 25 for 1.5 goals saved above expected. Over the full game SEA's 3.73 expected goals to CGY's 2.53 gave it a 69% chance of winning a replay of every shot, so Seattle was the better side. The score, though, was far wider than the chances.
